correctness.rationale: Define z=2u−1, h=z³−(15/28)z, d_epsilon=1+epsilon h, |epsilon|<28/13. Exact calculus gives |h|<=13/28, so quantile Q(u)=int_0^u dv/d(v) is increasing and finite with inverse F, density f(Q(u))=d(u)>0 analytic on interior. h is odd about u=1/2, hence d(1−u)≠d(u) for epsilon≠0, impossible for a symmetric absolutely continuous distribution. Substituting rho3=4u−3u² and reflected counterpart gives W3=(5z−3z³)/2; direct exact symbolic integration against h gives zero. For rho4=6u²−4u³, W4=6z−2z³, and int_0^1 W4h du=2/35, thus X_(1,4)=epsilon/35. Independent sympy integration reproduced W3/W4, 0 and 2/35; no finite experiment substitutes for the polynomial proof.

value.rationale: A proposed symmetry test can conflate a vanishing SINGLE population contrast with symmetry even when a full collection of contrasts characterizes symmetry.
